extracted.intended_audience: inventors, patent applicants, patent attorneys, patent office staff, and policymakers operating within the Cooperation Council for the Arab States of the Gulf (GCC)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards for patentability, filing, prosecution, rights, licensing, compulsory licensing, fees, administration, and enforcement of patents across GCC Member States under the GCC Patent Regulation and its Implementing Bylaws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention shall be patentable if it is new, involves an inventive step, industrially applicable and is not contrary to the laws of Islamic Shariya, or public order or to morality observed in the Cooperation Council States (Article 2/1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to new products, industrial processes, or manufacturing methods. See related provisions on novelty, inventive step, industrial applicability, and exceptions/exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty (definition and exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention is new if it is not anticipated by prior art, which consists of everything disclosed to the public anywhere by written or oral disclosure, by use, or by any other way realized before the relevant filing date or validly claimed priority date (Article 2/2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure within one year before filing/priority due to abusive actions by others is disregarded; disclosure at an officially recognized exhibition within six months preceding filing is not taken into account (Implementing Bylaws determine protection provisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step (non-obviousness)
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention involves an inventive step if, having regard to the relevant prior art, it would not have been obvious to a person having ordinary skill in the art (Article 2/3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard is a person having ordinary skill in the art; novelty alone is insufficient without inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention is industrially applicable if it can be produced or used in any type of industry, agriculture, fishing, or services (Article 2/4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industry is interpreted broadly to include handicraft; microbiological processes addressed elsewhere (Article 3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Security-related application procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application pertains to inventions connected with the security of any Cooperation Council State, procedures in the Implementing Bylaws shall apply (Article 2/5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special procedural rules may limit or alter prosecution, handling, or disclosure for security-sensitive inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-to-file rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Where more than one application pertains to the same invention, the patent shall be granted to the owner of the first application that has the earliest priority date (Article 2/6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority date (including valid priority claims) determines entitlement when multiple filings exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint inventorship and ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: If the invention results from joint efforts of several individuals, ownership of the patent belongs to them equally unless otherwise multilaterally agreed upon; a person is not an inventor if activities were limited to executing the ideas (Article 2/7/1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventorship is tied to contribution to inventive concept rather than mere execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee inventions and employer assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Right to a patent is assigned to the employer if the invention resulted from execution of a contract or obligation to carry out inventive activities, or if the inventor would not have achieved the invention without use of employer facilities, means, or information (Article 2/7/2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employee retains right to special remuneration determined by competent authority; agreements depriving employee of such rights are void. Applies to government employees. An application filed by employee within two years after termination is treated as filed during employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-patentable subject matter (general exclusions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The following shall not be regarded as inventions: discoveries, scientific theories, mathematical methods, and computer programs; schemes, rules, methods for doing business, performing purely mental acts, or playing games; plant varieties and species of animals and biological processes for production of plants or animals (except microbiological processes and their products); methods of surgical or therapeutic treatment and methods of diagnosis applied to the human or animal body (except products used in these methods) (Article 3/1 and 3/2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Microbiological processes and their products and tangible products used in excluded methods may be treated differently; patent protection for plant varieties/species is explicitly not provided by this Regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ministerial exclusion power for public interest
rubrics_metrics.description: The Ministerial Council may exclude from patentability some inventions whenever necessary to safeguard public order or morality, including protection of human, animal or plant life and health, or to avoid serious damage to the environment (Article 4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows policy-driven exclusions beyond general exclusions; scope and instances left to Ministerial Council decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file and required identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent application shall be submitted to the Office by the inventor, his registered agent, or his successor in title and be accompanied by the prescribed fee; application shall include names of applicant, inventor, and agent (if any), and where applicant is other than inventor a statement justifying applicant's right (Article 5/1/1-5/1/2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper identification and justification of entitlement required at filing to establish standing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Application shall relate only to one invention or to aspects so related as to constitute a single general inventive concept (Article 5/1/3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple unrelated inventions should be filed separately; unity affects formal examination and fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of application
rubrics_metrics.description: The application shall contain the title of the invention, a specification, one or more claims, one or more drawings (if any), and an abstract (Article 5/2/1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete set of documents required for formal filing and examination to proceed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient disclosure / enablement
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification shall disclose the invention in a manner sufficiently clear and complete for the invention to be carried out by a person having ordinary skill in the art (Article 5/2/2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enablement requirement supports validity; lack of sufficient disclosure may be ground for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims determine scope of protection
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim or claims shall determine the scope of the protection sought; the specification and the drawings may be used to interpret the claims (Article 5/2/3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims are primary for rights; specification/drawings are interpretive aids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim clarity, conciseness and support
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims shall be clear and concise and shall be fully supported by the specification (Article 5/2/4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lack of clarity or support can render claims invalid or rejectable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract purpose limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract shall merely serve the purpose of technical information and shall not be taken into account for interpreting the application (Article 5/2/5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract is informative only and not a substantive interpretive document for claim construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to provide additional information
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant shall provide the Office with the required additional information and data related to his application (Article 5/3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office can request further information during prosecution; failure to comply may affect prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may introduce amendments he deems fit if such amendments do not constitute a substantive modification to the contents of the original application (Article 5/4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments cannot add new matter beyond original disclosure; substantive changes are disallowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered agent requirement for non-residents
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant is a non-GCC resident, he shall appoint a registered agent who is a GCC resident to represent him before the Office (Article 6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local representation required for procedural acts and communications with the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claim requirements and term
rubrics_metrics.description: Application may contain claim of priority of previous application filed in any State or regional office; must indicate date and filing number and country and produce proof, otherwise priority claim denied; duration of priority shall be twelve Gregorian months (Article 7/1-7/2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict documentary proof required for priority; 12-month Paris Convention-style priority period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of application
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may withdraw his application at any time unless a final decision has been taken; withdrawal does not entitle reclaim of documents or refund of fees or expenses incurred (Article 8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal is allowed but fees and documents remain with Office; strategic withdrawal must consider consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date registration and substantive examination options
rubrics_metrics.description: Once application satisfies terms, the Office shall register the application filing date and formally examine it; substantive examination shall either be carried out by the Office or referred to one of the approved examination authorities after payment of the Substantive Examination fee (Article 9).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive examination may be outsourced; payment of substantive examination fee required for referral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal examination deficiency cure period
rubrics_metrics.description: If Formal Examination finds some prescribed terms missing, the Office may request completion within three months from notification; failure results in lapse (Article 10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three-month cure period strict; applications can lapse for non-response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant, publication and rejection procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If Substantive Examination finds application satisfies terms, Office grants patent, enters it in the register and publishes it and delivers Letters Patent three months from publication if no objection; if not eligible, Office rejects with reasons and publishes the decision (Article 11).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opposition/objection window tied to three months after publication; rejections are reasoned and published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of patent owner's exploitation rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent entitles owner to exploit invention: product exploitation includes manufacturing, use, import, sale, or offering for sale; for industrial processes owner also has rights to products directly obtained by using such process and to prevent others from actual use of the process without consent (Article 12/1-12/2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rights cover acts of exploitation broadly; process claims afford rights over direct product of the process as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior user defense / prior use continuation rights
rubrics_metrics.description: An establishment that in good faith manufactures, uses an industrial manufacturing process of a product, or makes serious preparations thereto, before the filing date or priority date of another's application shall have the right to continue such acts; assignment of the right only in conjunction with all elements of the business (Article 12/3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects bona fide prior users; rights tied to continuity and business transfer conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploitation obligation (working requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owner shall make sufficient exploitation of the patented invention in the Member States within three years from the date of grant; failure triggers compulsory licensing provisions (Article 13).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Working requirement aimed at local exploitation; insufficient exploitation can lead to compulsory license under Article 19.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted acts (research and temporary importation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rights do not extend to acts carried for scientific research purposes or use of patent articles on means of transportation temporarily or accidentally entering territories of Council States limited to necessities (Article 14/1-14/2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safe-harbours for research and transient use on vehicles; narrow in scope and limited to necessities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term length
rubrics_metrics.description: The term of a patent shall be twenty years counted from the date of filing the patent application (Article 15).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard 20-year term; no explicit mention here of extensions (e.g., for regulatory delays) — Bylaws may address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual maintenance fees and grace periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent subject to annual fee paid in advance starting from year following filing; failure to pay within three months allows additional three-month period with additional fee; failure to pay within six months from due date causes lapse; annual fees may be paid in advance to cover validity term; same provisions apply to applications; if Office delays decision >3 years applicant may abstain from payment until grant and then pay unpaid fees (Article 16).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Six-month total grace period includes surcharge; procedural relief if Office delay exceeds three years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and effect of licensing contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner may license others to perform exploitation acts; license must be in writing, signed by both parties, and authenticated by official authority in one of the Council States; licensing contract not effective vis-à-vis third parties unless entered in Office records and registration fees paid (Article 17/1-17/3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration confers effectiveness against third parties; contractual licenses can be non-exclusive and owner can continue exploiting unless contract says otherwise; licensee cannot assign rights unless expressly allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office control over license terms (anti-abuse/competition)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may request parties amend a licensing contract to rule out abuse of patent rights or negative influence on competition or possession/propagation of technology; failure to respond allows Office to deny approval and refuse registration (Article 18).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory oversight of licensing to preserve competition and technology dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds and conditions for compulsory license
rubrics_metrics.description: Where owner never exploited or insufficiently exploited the invention, Board may grant compulsory license observing: at least three years after grant; applicant must show efforts to obtain license under adequate compensation and fair terms; license not exclusive; essentially to meet local market demand; license decision defines scope/terms; adequate compensation to owner; exploitation limited to licensee; transfer only with business transfer and Board approval (Article 19/1-19/1/7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compulsory licence is remedial to address non-working; emphasis on prior negotiation and local market needs; compensation required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semiconductor technologies special restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: If the invention relates to 'semi-Conductors' technologies, licensing shall only be permitted for public, general, and non-commercial purposes, or to rectify non-competitive practices by judicial/administrative decisions (Article 19/2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stricter limits for semiconductors; licensing for commercial exploitation generally restricted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple compulsory licenses and emergency exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant of a compulsory license does not prevent other compulsory licenses; Board may disregard the 3-year and negotiation conditions if request due to state of emergency, dire public necessity, or for non-commercial use in one or more Council States; government agency requests for public interest may be approved per Article 19 terms (Article 20/1-20/3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows flexibility in emergencies, public interest, or non-commercial uses; multiple licenses possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory licensing for dependent patents
rubrics_metrics.description: If exploitation of an invention of significant technical advance and economic importance requires use of another invention, Board may grant a compulsory license to one or both parties unless they agree amicably, with Articles 19 and 20 observed (Article 21).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanism to resolve blocking/dependent patents to enable exploitation of improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation of compulsory license
rubrics_metrics.description: Compulsory license shall be cancelled if the beneficiary fails to exploit it sufficiently within two years (renewable once for legitimate reasons), fails to pay due amounts within three months of maturity, fails to satisfy other terms, or if circumstances that justified grant end and are unlikely to reoccur (Article 22/1-22/4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ongoing compliance and payment obligations; cancellation safeguards patent owner and market.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transferability and registration of ownership changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Ownership of patent and rights are transferable by inheritance or assignment wholly or partially; persons may request Office modification of particulars supported by evidential means; transfer not effective against others until registration and publication (Article 23/1-23/2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration is conclusive vis-à-vis third parties; evidentiary support required for modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals from Office decisions and Committee decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any decision by the Office may be appealed within three months from knowledge or publication; Implementing Bylaws provide proceedings before the Committee and fees; decisions of the Committee may be appealed before competent authority in host country according to that regulation or general rules (Article 24).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-tier internal appeal (Committee) and external national judicial/administrative appeal with time limits and procedures in Bylaws and national law.

rubrics_metrics.name: National competent authorities handle infringement disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: Competent authorities of each Member State shall examine disputes pertaining to infringement or imminent infringement and settle them pursuant to this Regulation and their own national patent regulations or general rules (Article 26).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforcement and remedies are primarily a national competence, applied consistently with GCC Regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register and official gazette obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office shall establish a register to enter patents and particulars in conformity with the Regulation and Bylaws and shall publish an official gazette for all publications stipulated (Article 27/1-27/2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public records and official publication mechanism required for legal effect and public notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance Committee composition and decision rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee shall consist of twelve members from Member States selected for personal capacity; each State nominates two members (one legal qualification, one technical specialist); members elect chairman and vice-chairman for three-year session; decisions by two-thirds majority of attendant members; meetings require at least one member from each State; postponement rules and neutrality obligations (Article 28/1-28/7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee structured to balance legal and technical expertise and ensure cross-state representation; neutrality and independence emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and filing restrictions for Office/Committee personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of the Committee, Board of Directors, and Patent Office staff may not during employment or for two years following termination submit applications on their behalf; information in their possession is regarded highly confidential (Article 29).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevent conflicts of interest and misuse of confidential information by staff and officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feeable acts and fee schedule authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Office shall collect fees for specified instances (filing, grant/publication, annual fees, amendments, delay fees, assignment, copies, compulsory license requests/grants, license registration, appeals, renewal of appeals, microorganism samples, temporary protection during exhibitions, patent search, substantive examination); such fees prescribed by Bylaws (Article 30).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive list of feeable services; exact amounts and procedures set in Implementing Bylaws.

rubrics_metrics.name: TRIPS exclusion term effect
rubrics_metrics.description: During the exclusion term, protection of products granted a patent by the Office shall not be valid in any Member State that is excluded in conformity with clause (4) of Article (65) of the TRIPS annexed to the WTO agreement (Article 31).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GCC Regulation observes TRIPS provisions and exclusions; national exclusions under TRIPS affect regional protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bylaws issuance authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The Ministerial Council shall issue the Bylaws of this Regulation (Article 32).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementing details, procedures, fees, and special rules are delegated to Bylaws issued by Ministerial Council.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation and amendment competency
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpretation and proposals of modification of this Regulation are competency of the Financial and Economic Cooperation Committee following coordination with the Scientific and Technical Cooperation Committee and Industrial Cooperation Committee (Article 33).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inter-committee coordination required for amendments and authoritative interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry into force timing
rubrics_metrics.description: This Regulation shall come into force three months from its publication and the publication of the Implementing Bylaws (Article 34).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective date contingent on both Regulation and Implementing Bylaws being published.
